about: A Nicaraguan cigar named for Luciano Meirelles, the blender behind Luciano Cigars (formerly ACE Prime). It started in 2020 as a single lancero and became a regular line with three thicker sizes in 2022.
notes: The maker lists the wrapper as Ecuadorian Habano Corojo 99; some early coverage called it Ecuadorian Sumatra. The maker lists the Belicoso as 5 x 50, while halfwheel listed it as 5 1/2 x 52 when it launched in 2022. The brand was sold under ACE Prime until 2022.
verifyNotes: Belicoso changed from 5 1/2 x 52 to the maker's 5 x 50, since the brief ranks the maker above halfwheel; the disagreement stays in notes. Wrapper and Medium-Full strength confirmed on the maker page. Country and factory come from halfwheel; the maker page does not name them.

about: A medium-strength blend from Luciano Meirelles whose Latin name means "let there be light." It pairs a high-priming Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with all-Nicaraguan binder and filler.
notes: Originally rolled in Nicaragua at Tabacalera Pichardo under the ACE Prime name. Production moved to Plasencia's Tabacos de Oriente in Danli, Honduras, with those cigars shipping from late 2024; the maker says the blend did not change.

about: A four-size line from Luciano Cigars, developed by Luciano Meirelles with sales manager Mike Dounoulis and retailer Frank Cossio of Astorian Cigar Co. It uses a double binder and filler from three countries and reached stores in April 2023.
notes: The maker gives no strength rating. Halfwheel's review of the Rothschild called it mild for most of the cigar, rising to medium at the end. Famous Smoke's spec table says Full while its description says medium-bodied.
verifyNotes: Blend, sizes, country and factory confirmed on the maker's press page and halfwheel. Strength left null: the maker publishes none and the other sources conflict. Swapped the halfwheel shipping news for the maker page and Famous Smoke in sources and added the Famous Smoke conflict to notes.

about: The original Macanudo blend and one of the best-selling premium cigars in the United States, made by General Cigar. It is a mellow Connecticut Shade cigar often suggested to new smokers.
notes: The maker lists 21 sizes; ten common ones are shown here. Macanudo was once made in Jamaica and is now rolled in the Dominican Republic.
verifyNotes: Reworded the Jamaica note to match what the sources say. The maker lists body as Mellow, taken as Mild, and Famous Smoke also lists Mild. The 1968 start year is not on the listed pages; it is supported by the maker's Macanudo 1968 page and halfwheel's report of the brand's 50th anniversary in 2018.

wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Shade "Capa Especial" (first and second primings)
binder: Mexico (San Andrés, first and second primings)
about: A seasonal Macanudo that uses golden Connecticut Shade wrapper from the lowest primings of the plant, which the maker says gives extra natural sweetness. It first appeared in 2002 and comes back once a year.
notes: Released once a year in a limited run, so it can be out of stock between releases. The size list changes a little each year; the sizes here are the 2026 release.

about: The lighter of two Inspirado blends Macanudo launched in the U.S. in 2017. It has an aged Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and no Dominican tobacco in the blend.
notes: The maker calls it mellow to medium; Famous Smoke lists it as Medium. The maker names Esteli for part of the Nicaraguan filler, while halfwheel and Cigar Dojo say Condega. Halfwheel reported the Corona size is rolled at STG Danli in Honduras.

about: The darker partner to Inspirado White, launched in the U.S. in 2017 with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over Nicaraguan filler. It was pitched as a bolder cigar than the classic Macanudo lines.
notes: A different cigar also called Inspirado Black, with a Connecticut Habano wrapper, was sold in Europe from 2015. Sizes are from the maker; halfwheel's 2017 list had the Robusto at 4 7/8 x 48 and the Toro at 5 7/8 x 54.

binder: USA (Connecticut Broadleaf, aged in Cabernet barrels)
filler: Brazil (Mata Fina), Dominican Republic (Olor, Piloto Cubano), Nicaragua (Jalapa)
about: A limited Macanudo series made with Flint Knoll Winery of Napa Valley. The Broadleaf binder is aged in French oak barrels that held the winery's Cabernet Sauvignon.
notes: The current Estate Reserve is three limited releases with Flint Knoll: No. 1 (2022), No. 2 (2023) and No. 3 (2024), all the same basic blend. Earlier, unrelated limited editions also used the Estate Reserve name around 2014 and 2015.

about: The dark-wrapper version of the classic Macanudo, finished in Connecticut Broadleaf. It stays on the mellow side for a maduro.
notes: The maker calls it mellow to medium; Famous Smoke lists it as Medium.
verifyNotes: Binder changed from 'USA (Connecticut)' to 'Connecticut': the maker lists only 'Connecticut' and does not say where the leaf is grown.

about: A medium-bodied Macanudo with an Ecuadorian Habano wrapper over a Dominican binder and filler from three countries. The maker cites a 91 rating from Cigar Aficionado.
notes: Famous Smoke describes the binder as Brazilian Mata Fina; the maker lists a Dominican La Vega Especial binder with the Brazilian leaf in the filler.
verifyNotes: Rewrote 'about' to drop a comparison with the Café that the sources do not make. Country confirmed on Famous Smoke; the maker page does not state it.

about: The first Inspirado, sold only in Europe and Canada from 2014 before reaching U.S. shops in 2016. It is made in Honduras with a Honduran wrapper and binder.
notes: Strength is described differently: the maker says Medium, halfwheel called it medium-full and Famous Smoke lists Full. Famous Smoke also lists the Dominican Republic as origin, but the maker and halfwheel say it is made in Honduras.

about: A Nicaraguan-made Inspirado released in 2018 for Macanudo's 50th anniversary. It uses filler tobaccos aged five, ten and twelve years under an Ecuadorian Habano ligero wrapper.
notes: Unlike most Macanudos, it is rolled in Nicaragua rather than the Dominican Republic. Halfwheel listed all three launch sizes as box pressed.

about: An Inspirado built around South American tobacco, with a Brazilian Arapiraca wrapper and Colombian filler. It reached stores in 2020.

wrapperLeaf: Connecticut Shade grown in Bahia, Brazil
filler: Brazil (Mata Fina), Nicaragua (Jalapa), Dominican Republic (Piloto Cubano, Cubita from Mao)
about: A limited Inspirado wrapped in Connecticut-seed shade tobacco grown in Bahia, Brazil, which is an unusual place to grow that leaf. It came out in 2021 and returned in 2024.
notes: Limited edition: 2,000 boxes of Toro and 1,500 of Churchill in 2021, then a second run in 2024. The maker's page also shows a 6 1/4 x 52 Torpedo.

about: A 2019 take on the Macanudo Café blend that swaps the U.S. Connecticut Shade wrapper for Ecuadorian Connecticut and adds Nicaraguan filler. General Cigar described it as creamy and medium-bodied.
notes: It no longer appears on the maker's website, so it may be out of production. Check stock before promising it.

about: Macanudo Vintage is a series of cigars built around a wrapper crop from one standout year. The current Connecticut Shade edition is Vintage 2010, whose wrapper was aged for about a decade.
notes: Vintage is a series, and each year's edition is its own blend. Details here are for Vintage 2010, which shipped in 2021. The maker also sells Vintage Maduro 2013 with a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. The maker calls Vintage 2010 mellow to medium; Famous Smoke lists Medium.

about: A coffee-infused cigar and the first flavored Macanudo, launched in 2018 for the brand's 50th anniversary. It is hand rolled with an Indonesian wrapper, a Philippine binder and Nicaraguan filler.
notes: This is a flavored (infused) cigar. It launched simply as M by Macanudo; the maker now calls it M by Macanudo Coffee since other flavors have joined the family.
verifyNotes: Rewrote 'about': the long-filler versus short-filler claim is not stated on either source.

about: A darker, fuller Macanudo named for the year the brand started. It debuted in August 2008 as a break from the mellow Café style.
notes: The maker rates it medium to full; Famous Smoke lists it as Medium.
verifyNotes: Replaced the Inspirado Green review in sources with the halfwheel page carrying General Cigar's statement that 1968 debuted in August 2008. Set wrapperCategory to Habano because Famous Smoke describes the wrapper as Honduran San Agustin Havana-seed. Trimmed 'about' to match.

about: A full-strength Man O' War blend made by AJ Fernandez in Esteli, Nicaragua, using high-priming ligero filler under an oily Ecuadorian Habano wrapper. Man O' War is a Cigars International brand.
notes: Famous Smoke lists it as Full, while Blind Man's Puff reviewers rated it medium-strong.
verifyNotes: Removed the note about a Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper in Famous Smoke's blurb: the page does not mention it. Replaced it with the strength difference between sources.

about: The mild member of the Man O' War family, made by AJ Fernandez with an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over Nicaraguan tobacco. A small amount of ligero in the filler keeps some of the brand's character.
notes: Man O' War is a Cigars International brand, so most shops will not carry it. Blend and sizes here come from one retailer, CigarPlace, whose table lists a Nicaraguan binder while its write-up says the cigar is bound in Ecuadorian Connecticut.

about: A small, strong Nicaraguan puro that AJ Fernandez is said to have first blended for himself. It is a 5 x 42 corona with a pigtail cap and unfinished foot.
notes: Sold in two wrappers: a natural Nicaraguan Habano and a Habano Maduro. Blind Man's Puff rated the Maduro medium-strong rather than full.

about: The top-of-the-line Man O' War, made by AJ Fernandez in small yearly batches with a dark Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper over Nicaraguan ligero. It costs well above the rest of the brand.
notes: Strength is described inconsistently: CigarPlace's spec table says Medium while its write-up calls it full-bodied, and Bespoke Unit rates the body medium to full. Bespoke Unit describes the wrapper as Sumatra Maduro and says about 10,000 are made a year.
